Summary of practice

1. Listen to the Humility and Service lesson audio. You may want to listen more
than once.

2. Adopt an attitude and mindset of service where and when you can. Practice
generosity, without going so far that you overextend yourself to self-sabotage.

3. Watch for how your characters react with their princess attitudes, and
sense of entitlement, judgments etc. Write out the inventory of beliefs that show up
to resist. Be skeptical of them. By putting yourself in a state of service your characters will
react, get loud, and expose themselves with their stories and emotional reactions.
Humility and service practice is an opportunity to reveal and cleanse your self
importance. So, by serving others, you are serving your authentic self, Truth, and Love.



Some notes

Service is a fast way to crush your self importance. What is self importance? It is your ego.
It is the resistance, frustrations, expectations of your villain, princess, hero, victim, and
judge all rolled together.

This session is about crushing those grandiose thoughts and self images. Service is an
attitude, mindset, and practice to take on personal growth of consciousness against your
ego.

Service is also a way to benefit others. When you benefit others, you are different. You
practice giving. You can give because you have enough for your self first, and have enough
to give to others. With this attitude that you have more than enough for your self, you can
be generous. Being generous is a way to expand your sense of confidence, and abundance.

Having a sense of abundance increases your gratitude, and you can be more generous. By
being generous you create relationships where others trust you and know they will not be
taken advantage of.

By building trust they are more likely to include you in future opportunities.





                                                                                                               1/2

This practice of service asks you to put yourself in the viewpoint of other people. This goes
back to the viewpoint practice. Noticing when another driver is trying to get into your
lane, and giving them space is an act of service. It’s an easy shift because we have all tried
to get over to another lane at some time in our life.

There is a fine line between an act of service done with humility and one done from self
importance, such as from the hero or pleaser/prostitute. The action may be just the same,
but the feeling and attitude is different.

Common Questions

   selfmastery.mn.co/posts/self-mastery-course-ii-common-questions-6431820

Is it possible that an action can be both from humility and self
importance?

Yes. This is very often the case. When I was teaching I was helping people clear up their
false beliefs and emotions. I was in service. At the same time I had stories about how great
I was doing and had images in my mind of grandiosity.

This didn’t mean that I stopped teaching because it was corrupt. I was both in service, and
my ego was going along and trying to stitch in stories and beliefs that were false at the
same time.

I kept teaching, and kept hunting my self importance at the same time. The process
allowed me to slowly whittle away at self importance by watching it show up all the time.



How can I practice service?

Get a trash bag, or a shopping bag and go for a walk. Pick up the trash you see along your
walk. Dispose of it properly. Wear some gloves if you like.

Does a voice come out and comment about how dirty this is? Are you too good to pick up
trash? Are you better than the person that picks up trash? Why should they do it?

Does a voice come out being embarrassed because you look like a homeless person
worried what others will think?

Or does a voice come out hoping others will notice what you are doing because it is so
conscious?



How can I practice service?

Perhaps you live in a city where there are regularly homeless people. When you are out to
dinner, order an extra meal to go. Then offer it to a homeless person on the street.



How can I practice service?

Cook dinner for your partner, or your family.

IF you live alone, invite a friend over and cook a meal for them.



                                                                                                               1/2

You are also creating connections, trust, and community.

Maybe you already are doing many things, but you didn’t look at them this way?

Hello this is Gary van Warmerdam with the Pathway to Happiness audio series and Self-
mastery. Today’s topic is about service and the intent for this topic of service, this practice
of service comes about twofold. One is it’s about crushing the remnants, the last details of
self-importance. Self-importance being any beliefs we hold where we are better than
someone else or the belief that we hold that we are less than someone else. And we will go
about this by putting ourselves in the action of service because at a certain point you can’t
really solve that thing in the mind by thinking about it and the very problem is created of
thinking it can be solved by thinking. So action of service is how to go about that and
break it through action.

The second aspect of service after crushing self-importance is to understand how service
plays a role in creating prosperity and abundance and manifesting what you want and
creating a life that you want. First I want to cover two different paradigms of service and
when I talk about service I am talking about the role people play with each other. You
could say the role is servant to master but also employee to boss, teacher to student. These
kinds of roles where people are in service, working for each other, helping each other, how
we typically think of service is we hire a landscaper to clean up our yard and they do our
tree service, they do our lawn service and they are in service to us.

We can look at it and say from our point of view we are their boss, the boss and employee
relationship looks the same. That employee works for the boss and does what the boss
says. What if we shift that a little bit and we see what we do for the landscaper. When we
hire that landscaper for the person to clip our trees and cut our grass we provide them
with payment, then we are serving them so that they can feed their family. Then at the
same time they’re doing a service for us we are doing service for them, it’s in exchange. It
looks inequitable because of the appearance of who has power and it looks like somebody
is less than someone else in the power structure of things but that’s only a structure that
happens in the mind.

If we look at a classroom of students that teacher is telling the students what to do and
giving them instructions. Then it looks like the teacher is the master but in a way that
teacher is really instructing the students and guiding them then the teacher is the servant
serving those students, guiding them to grow and towards wisdom and function in the
world or understanding calculus whatever the relationship is. Then it’s not a dominant
authoritarian role. Even though they have the authority, they have more power, they are
also doing more service.

There is a story of the far-off land in the Zen monastery and the young man who travels
many miles to go to this Zen monastery he wants to be a monk and apprentice and
become a Zen master and he arrives there late in the evening and it’s cold because it’s way
up in the mountains and he goes knocking on the door and asked to enter and a person
comes to the gates and say what are you doing here. The young man says I want to



                                                                                                               1/9

apprentice, I want to be a monk and the man on the other side of the gate said you have
no business here, go away and the boy keeps knocking and the man returns and says go
away and a couple of hours go by and it’s now very dark and the man’s knocking and
pounding on the gate to get in and the man says look you cannot stay here tonight this is
no place for you.

You do not have what it takes to be here but since you’re so persistent and now it’s too late
for you to travel anywhere here’s some blankets so you can get through the night but in
the morning you must go and in the morning the man’s knocking at the door again and
the monk comes to the gate and the young man says I want to be an apprentice, I want to
become a Zen monk and this kind of thing goes on for two or three days with the young
man outside the gate being told he has no business being there, he is not ready until
finally after three days people behind the gate finally say you know, you’re too stubborn to
go away and too stupid to listen to us. You have no business here but since you won’t go
away, least we can do is put you to work. You cannot apply to be a Zen monk.

It is not going to happen but if you want you can stay here and you can help clean the
floors, wash the clothes and the young man agrees and they give him all the menial tasks
of washing clothes, cleaning dishes and he periodically asks if he can apprentice there and
become a monk and they tell him no, no, absolutely not, you do not have what it takes to
be a monk. This is not for you and he goes on about his tasks and perhaps in the story in a
person’s mind he becomes angry, he becomes frustrated, he becomes judgmental of these
Zen teachers.

They look to be cruel and mean to him and if he believes his judgments he won’t survive
and he will get tired of his work and he’ll leave but if he’s able to continue about his work
and his duties and hold his judgments at bay to a point where he doesn’t believe them
then he can start to enjoy his work and can enjoy washing the floors, chopping the wood,
carrying the water, cleaning the clothes and in that joy in his work, the more he finds that,
the more he will have crushed his self-importance, the more he will beat down the stories
in his mind that say these guys don’t know what they’re talking about, I can do this, I can
be a great monk, I can be a great Zen master.

All those stories of being better of all these great things he envisions for himself, these are
self-important stories and so in his mind it’s a war. The teachers have given him the
action, wash the clothes, clean the dishes and they treat him as a lowly servant. They
haven’t even given him the status of apprentice monk. What the practice doesn’t know is
they are teaching him. They are teaching and testing him at the same time. They’re
putting in front of his face by giving him all these menial tasks an opportunity for him to
see all his self-importance.

They get to test also his desire that she really want to be there or is he going to give up and
quit because if he gives up and quits in two or three or six months it was a waste of the
teachers time anyways but if he can survive the six months to a year, the two or three
years and in that process he breaks free of all his self-importance, his personal reactions





                                                                                                               2/9

of being treated like a servant, if he’s able to break free of his self-importance and enjoy
his work, all the judgment stories, images of what he should be and how he should be
treated with so much more respect.

If he’s able to break that he can last there in the monastery doing his tasks, he will pass his
initiation test, which is he will respect himself more, respect his teachers more instead of
belief judgments about himself, victim stories about himself or how they’re treating him.
You see as soon as he knocked on the gate his apprenticeship began but they didn’t tell
him. They were teaching him from the very beginning, they were serving him, they were
serving him by pinning him against his own self-importance and seeing how he doesn’t
have 10:06 .

From the very beginning those Zen teachers and those Zen masters are setting up
situations where this young man has an opportunity to break his self-importance. Then
you could say those teachers are serving him and the young apprentice is doing the dirty
dishes, he’s doing the laundry and it looks like he’s in doing all these menial tasks he’s a
servant, even a slave to these teachers but from a teacher point of view what they are
giving this man is a much more valuable opportunity. They are giving him the opportunity
to break his self-importance, to break all his judging victim stories, to break his false
images of himself and the images he projects on this path.

From the point of view of menial tasks it looks like the young man is the servant. It looks
like he’s disrespected but from the point of view of the teacher, teacher is the servant and
this man is his master that he serves and he’s giving to his master the keys to his personal
freedom. He is giving to his master the tools for his personal freedom, the opportunity to
break free of his ego. If we look at the relationship this way we see that the great
opportunity for crushing our self-importance is if we put ourselves in the role of a servant
when we let other people’s dictates be more important than our own.

This is crushing our own self-importance, it’s challenging our own self-importance like in
the case of that young man. His agenda was that he’ll be a monk. That was, what he
thought was important what he was there for. When he was able to put his agenda aside,
which is to say put all his projections of himself aside and what he thought would be right
how he felt he should be treated and instead just be in service to those in front of hm, now
he became a monk. Is just that it wasn’t what he thought it was supposed to be then this is
what we can do with ourselves without having to go to a monastery.

We can put ourselves in service to other people in a way that it can crush our self-
importance. It’s going to push it to the surface. if we no longer push our agenda of what’s
right and how things are supposed to be but listen to others and allow ourselves to serve
their agenda there’s going to be an opportunity to see all our reactions, which is all the
places we are attached to, what we believe is right, how things are supposed to be and yes
is going to create a conflict and your opportunity then is to see where your self-
importance comes up. This is how we’ll use putting ourselves in the action of service to
other people to expose our self-importance.





                                                                                                               3/9

If we are an employee we put ourselves in service to our boss. This isn’t a big shift in what
we do but it may be a shift in our mental attitude, a chance for us to see the stories where
we think our idea is better than theirs and understand service can take a thousand
different forms and we are going to look for in the smallest of places and give you a couple
examples.

The boss I was working for one day got upset at me. I had missed a follow-up on a client
or he perceives that I’d missed a follow up on a client. I hardly recall it now but I know it
wasn’t what he thought it was. Anyways he had a big emotional reaction, the biggest one
I’d seen him have with me and I knew nothing was out of sorts with this client but in that
moment I decided to serve my boss. If I took the point of view, wait a minute, you don’t
understand, this is what’s going on I’m basically telling my boss he’s wrong and at the
moment my perception was he wouldn’t hear it. It would just upset him more.

So in service to my boss and strangely enough in service to myself so I didn’t exacerbate a
volatile situation, I put on the emotion of remorse which I could do easily because I
practice shifting my motions at will. I became apologetic. I told him I’d go figure out what
happened and figure out what needed to be done and get back to him. He got to vent, he
got to believe he was right and I got to get out of there sooner instead of arguing with him
then I chose to serve in that way. I went back to my office, I followed up with the client. I
found out what they need, what’s going on with the questions, I get back and report to my
boss later in the day.

He feels much better and we didn’t have a disagreement in perception about what he
thought and what I thought. I didn’t push my own agenda now understand there are times
when I would serve my boss by pushing my agenda, what I felt was really best for him and
what was best for the company and he tell me to do something and I tell him why it was a
bad idea. I would disagree and give my point of view. In that process I wouldn’t make his
point of view wrong but I would share my point of view, why I think it works this way but
this is a kind of service also. Sometimes the best service you can give is to disagree.
There’s not an exact rule or law what service is but if he’s about to do something you step
off a curb in the traffic, then sometimes the best thing you can do with someone is to grab
them and yank them and tell them later by the way there’s a car then service takes billions
of different forms, billions of different forms and each moment is its own creation and has
its own most impeccable way of going about it.

There’s no right answer, there’s no wrong answer. One day the janitor came into take out
the trash and I realized that my trashcan was in the side of my desk that was farthest away
from the door walking in and out and I realized it will be easier if my trashcan is on the
door side of my desk and I moved my trashcan a little bit of service to make his job easier.
An aspect of this kind of service, isn’t it moving the trash can was a big deal but part of
that required me stepping out of my point of view of what was convenient for me and
looking at things from his point of view and what would make things easier for him.
Giving up my own personal point of view and taking on someone else’s point of view it’s
an expansion of consciousness, expansion towards compassion and allows us to be a
better servant, even to see someone else’s needs before they realize that they would be
better off what would even ask for something.


                                                                                                               4/9

If there’s another driver and they’re trying to wedge in the traffic in your lane, make a
space and let them in. That’s an active service, that’s putting someone else in a way that
they are ahead of you not because they’re better than you. No, just doing the opportunity
to expose your stories of self-importance. You see, in this way you take on this action of
service not just to serve other people but you’re serving yourself in the way you put
yourself in the role of that Zen monk apprentice. You’re serving yourself but this time you
know what you’re doing and you know why. That young apprentice Zen monk he didn’t
know why, he didn’t know he was in school already but with you, you can do it with
awareness and know why you’re doing what you’re doing.

You are both going to serve another person but principally serve yourself by exposing your
self-importance. You know, if you don’t want to make a gap in the lane for another driver,
what is that story? What is your resistance? What is your hesitation? What makes you
believe that you need to get there faster than them? That your destination and your arrival
time is more important than theirs? You see, that’s your story that comes from self-
importance if you have that, then by doing the exact opposite of that story which is to let
another driver in, you are breaking that story, that belief that it’s more important for me
to get there on time than for them to get there on time. There’s something very important
to understand about service.

In those old archetype versions, we can do a lot of service for other people in a way that is
self-abusive. Our prostitute and our hero roles are often about doing good for other
people in order to get external rewards from other people, to get praise, to get acceptance,
to get love to get respect. This isn’t that kind of service. That kind of service is self-abusive
to get recognition, to get praise, that’s not service, not for someone else. That’s trying to
serve your own self-importance, your own victim your own judge, your own hero
archetypes, yes you are in service but you’re in service to your archetype characters, not to
you and not to anybody else, then that real service isn’t about recognition. If you find you
need a story to get recognized is a good way to see your self-importance.

Then when you see it, expose it and you do the exact opposite by doing something in a
way that doesn’t get you any recognition and you get to watch that story really get
agitated, exposed and finally pop. You have to resist temptation to try and get attention
for your service. Though stories will want you to get recognized and this is the exact intent
of putting yourself in service to other people you are going to expose those stories, they’re
going to become agitated. The dream where this can be corrupted, the near enemies of
this approach is where we fall to those temptations and we start serving our archetypes
instead of someone else and we start serving our archetypes instead of our authentic self
because by trying to find and crush your self-importance you are serving your authentic
self not your judging victim.

Another danger in this process though is if we take service too far. If we take service too
far to where we are trying to take care of other people’s needs to the point where we
become exhausted, tired and depleted or we take care of other people’s needs in a way
that they take advantage of us. If someone feels very needy for attention that we might





                                                                                                               5/9

feel like we’re serving them by giving them a lot of attention so they feel better then
there’s a fine line between giving them attention to the point where it helps them and
giving them attention in a way that helps them but also drains us.

You see at a certain point if you’re trying to satisfy their archetype characters of neediness
that come from a victim you can give all your energy and it still might not make a
difference. In that way, it’s like putting all your resources down the drain, you put all your
energy there and there’s no benefit for you or for them. This is in service. You’re not really
helping anybody, you’re not really getting results and all you’re doing is draining your
own resources. When you become exhausted and then you can’t help yourself as well and
you can’t help other people as well then part of being a good servant is taking care of
yourself. Knowing what your needs are and making sure that you are taking care of, you
are healthy, you have enough sleep, you have enough exercise and rest you have healthy
food so that you can better serve yourself and others.

If I’m going to be the best employee for my boss then I want to make sure that I take good
care of my physical health. I am going to make sure that if I’m sick I go see a doctor or
take care of my body and get rest so that yes I may miss one day but I can be there the
whole following week. Then this is a balance and is not a black or white but is to help you
to see that there’s other ways of looking and evaluating these things. As you practice this
exercise of service to others remember one of the goals here, one of the intents here is that
you are serving yourself. You are serving yourself by taking these actions to serve others,
to see if any self-importance reaction shows up. That way you can clean that up, you can
identify the story and belief behind that. Then this active service, in a way it’s like you’re
putting yourself in that Zen monastery and everyone around you is the teacher and you
get an opportunity to expose your beliefs and your dreams of self-importance. You don’t
need a Zen teacher to do that. You can do that yourself.

Here’s the other half of this exercise about service. Service is also about prosperity and
this has a lot to do with creating what you want whether it’s a huge dream or a little
dream. Somewhere in this process you’re probably going to be interacting with other
people, if you act in a way of service to them you will find that they respond a whole lot
better to you, bringing that attitude of no self-importance which is to say an attitude of
humility allows for an open interchange of dialogue, communication, problem solving
that makes for great accomplishments. When I talk about creating what you want and
we’ll talk about this in a realm of prosperity, if you look at the people who’ve prospered
greatly, by that I suggest reading Napoleon Hill’s “Think and grow rich”, big study of very
wealthy people Henry Ford, Carnegie, Firestone people like that, anyhow.

One of the things we can point to with people who have created huge wealth is that they
served people. It may not always be obvious but you cannot be in charge of a large
company or large organization without being in service to them. Let’s take Bill Gates,
whether you like him or whether you hate him, whether you think he’s the devil or not,
the point is his company writes checks to pay employees every week for the work they do
so they can feed their family and provide for themselves, healthcare, insurance all these
things. Then he has to make sure that his thousands and thousands of people are taking
care of, that their money gets to their bank account on time. He has customers that buy


                                                                                                               6/9

his products and he has to make sure that he delivers a quality product that helps his
customer. If it doesn’t help his customer then he’s not providing good service through that
product. Then he’s not being a good servant. Looks like he’s a very powerful man but he’s
a very powerful man because he’s serving many, many people.

When the time comes and he stops being a good servant to all those people, they stop
buying his products, they don’t listen to what he says, they don’t care what he says, and he
destroys the relationship he has with them. Then this relationship of service, where you
do things that benefit other people, whether you provide them a product, you provide
them a service, you cut their lawn, you provide them some self-help audiotape, the higher
quality service that you provide the more you can be rewarded, the more people want your
service, the more people want you as their servant. Then looks like you’re more powerful
but all you are is a bigger servant but is also more people you can serve in that way where
you provide something valuable then the more people will pay you for your services and
your products and this is how you can prosper.

You prosper by providing value, you prosper by providing good service. People will come
back to you again and again. For reading about providing great service from a CEO,
president, leader of an organization role I suggest the book “Good to Great” by Jim
Collins. He describes different kinds of leadership, specifically two different kinds, he
talks about a level for leadership and this is the big leaders you see of Lee Iacocca type
personalities, larger-than-life personalities that we think of great leaders in business,
dynamic leaders and visionaries but then he described a different kind of leader, a leader
called a level five leader which almost is the reverse. They aren’t big and flashy and there
aren’t many articles written about them and they don’t write books and they are very quiet
people.

They are very quiet people because they are humble and by humble I don’t mean meek.
Humble, quiet they listen more than they talk, they don’t push their agenda, they ask a lot
of questions and they gleaned from all these people around them, ideas and by not
pushing their agenda people have an open space to communicate and whole different
paradigms are exposed and this kind of teamwork that comes about in this environment
that humble people create becomes powerful. This is specific dynamic of leadership in
great companies that he described, not just good companies but great long-term
companies. These people are humble and not meek. They create powerful organizations
that do a lot of good. They take great care of their employees, which is they are great
servants to their employees. They are great servants to their customers and their
companies prosper.

What is important to notice about these great leaders of companies is they didn’t get their
humility in the job. They had it before they got there. Some point in their lives they crush
their self-importance or just never really built that much of it, that in order to be in a
place of power and not have that power corrupt you is important that you crush your self-
importance. You will find all the places it shows up. It’s easier to do it before you get there
because once you’re there that power can blind you. If you’re there and you’re going to do
it then you have to work a little harder and when I talk about humility with power, two




                                                                                                               7/9

examples Nelson Mandela, a very powerful leader but he didn’t put himself ahead of the
people he served. He didn’t feel that anybody on the other side needed to be punished,
there needed to be restitution, redemption more than anybody needed to be right.

Gandhi. Here’s an example of a humble man and yet incredibly powerful. Powerful
because he worked to serve people, not big powerful, important people but the common
people and there’s a whole lot more of them and so his power became great. There’s
nothing meek about these guys. Their influence and what they suggest and the power to
influence people comes from the fact that people trust them, people trust them because
they see they will be served by these humble people. Which means less self-importance,
more you can accomplish and the less likelihood it will become corruptive once you build
it.

Self-importance has nothing to do with greatness, real greatness except that crushing self-
importance gives you an opportunity to do great things. Something you understand about
humility, self-importance. Self-importance is focused on being something, is focused on
accomplishing something, whereas service is focused on the doing of something. It’s on
the attitude. Something to notice about these people, these great servants, captains of
industry, leaders like Gandhi and Mandela, being a servant and we can throw in there the
Dalai Lama because he’s in service to his people and all his followers and it looks like he’s
a leader and has powerful influence.

From another point of view he’s a powerful leader because he serves many, many people
without any real self-importance about what he’s doing. The thing is about being in
service to people and why it can be such a pleasure is it’s a way you can express your love
to them, sharing with someone your love with them is one of the greatest pleasures you
will experience in your life. Then if you can write a check to your employees, use that as an
opportunity to love them and care for them, the way you feed your children you are
helping them feed their children. If you have a boss, doing something for them can be an
act of love for them, an act of gratitude towards them, doing the report by the time it’s
due, opening up a space to let the other driver in and you can do it with an attitude of love
and respect for them.

Recognize that doing acts of service doesn’t have anything to do with being weak or
menial. Cleaning the floors and doing the laundry, you can do with incredible respect for
yourself, respect for others. It can be an act of love for other people, an act of love for
yourself and the thing about doing them, whether it’s taking out the trash for somebody to
weigh the sale of you is to make their life easier and serve them in that way. No matter
how menial a task, it doesn’t have anything to do with disrespecting yourself. No matter
how humble your engagement with people, it doesn’t have anything to do with
disrespecting yourself or allowing other people to disrespect you.

Then real humility isn’t about being better than someone else, is not about being less than
someone else. It’s about realizing everybody is the same and you respect yourself with an
incredible amount of intensity and you bring that intensive respect and you respect other





                                                                                                               8/9

people in that same way. In this way no one is better than you and no one is worse than
you and you’re not better than anybody else and you are not worse than anybody else,
equal level of respect for all people. This is where there’s no self-importance.

If you find that you’re working for someone in a job and they disrespect you, you work for
them, you give a lot to them and they don’t notice and they don’t appreciate it then you
find out they are really not respecting you. You bring it to their attention and they don’t
pay you well enough or what have you. They aren’t treating you well, they aren’t a good
servant back to you then it may be time to find another boss. One that will treat you with
more respect, one that understands that they are also in the role of service because the
